overview: Arta-dhyana, in Jain philosophy, refers to a form of disturbed or sorrowful meditation characterized by negative states of mind such as grief, sorrow, and anxiety. It is one of the four types of dhyana (meditation) outlined in Jain texts, which also include dharma-dhyana (righteous meditation), raudra-dhyana (passionate meditation), and shukla-dhyana (pure meditation). Arta-dhyana is considered a non-beneficial form of meditation as it is associated with attachment and aversion, leading to karmic bondage. It often arises from personal distress, fear of loss, or attachment to worldly possessions. According to Jain teachings, overcoming arta-dhyana is essential for spiritual progress and liberation.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Arta-dhyana is the engagement of the mind with objects of sorrow and distress.
primary_sources.notes: The Tattvartha Sutra is a foundational Jain text that systematically presents the core teachings of Jainism. Arta-dhyana is distinguished as a state to transcend in the pursuit of moksha (liberation).

misconceptions.myth: Arta-dhyana is a form of positive meditation leading to liberation.
misconceptions.reality: Arta-dhyana is actually a negative form of meditation associated with sorrow and distress, which hinders spiritual progress.
